g.text: Which change clears the Vancouver example?

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #54635e

g.text: Two earners: CAD 150,000 gross income, CAD 100,000 liquid cash, CAD 500 monthly existing debt.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e

g.text: Each change is applied separately to the same 2023 price/rate baseline with current rules. A 20% lower purchase price clears both modeled checks in

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e

g.text: this example; the other displayed changes leave an income shortfall. The HBP case moves CAD 40,000 of existing, separately assumed RRSP assets into

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e

g.text: purchase cash and requires future repayment. No price/rate forecast or loan approval is made.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #54635e

g.text: Kevin Yamada | Canadian Household Finance | Official Canadian public sources
